אָמַ֙רְתָּ֙ אֽוֹי־נָ֣א לִ֔י כִּֽי־יָסַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה יָג֖וֹן עַל־מַכְאֹבִ֑י יָגַ֙עְתִּי֙ בְּאַנְחָתִ֔י וּמְנוּחָ֖ה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי׃ ס
This is what you are to say to him:[^4] This is what the LORD says: What I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting, the whole land.[^5]
כֹּ֣ה ׀ תֹּאמַ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּנִ֙יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י הֹרֵ֔ס וְאֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־נָטַ֖עְתִּי אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֑שׁ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ הִֽיא׃

And you, are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am going to bring disaster on all humankind,[^6] declares the LORD, but I will let you escape with your life[^7] wherever you go.

וְאַתָּ֛ה תְּבַקֶּשׁ־לְךָ֥ גְדֹל֖וֹת אַל־תְּבַקֵּ֑שׁ כִּ֡י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא רָעָ֤ה עַל־כָּל־בָּשָׂר֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֨י לְךָ֤ אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל עַ֥ל כָּל־הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלֶךְ־שָֽׁם׃ ס

n.1: Literally "from the mouth of Jeremiah".
n.2: In 605 BC, the year Baruch wrote the scroll described in 36:1–8.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: The LORD now speaks to Jeremiah, telling him what to say to Baruch.
n.5: Literally "and the whole land, it". See 1:10.
n.6: Literally "all flesh".
n.7: Literally "I will give you your life as plunder" (21:9).

v: The word of the LORD[^1] that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.[^2]
אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

Concerning Egypt. About the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:[^3]

לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל־חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה עַל־נְהַר־פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
Prepare shield and buckler,[^4] and advance to battle!
עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
Harness the horses; mount, you horsemen![^5] Take your positions with helmets on! Polish the spears; put on your armor!
אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכֽוֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת׃
Why do I see them terrified, falling back? Their warriors are beaten down; they flee headlong and do not look back. Terror on every side![^6] declares the LORD.
מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
The swift cannot flee, nor the warrior escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
אַל־יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל־יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֙וֹנָה֙ עַל־יַ֣ד נְהַר־פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ׃
Who is this, rising like the Nile,[^7] like rivers whose waters surge?
מִי־זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו׃
Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, "I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy cities and those who live in them."
מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה־אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
Go up, you horses! Drive furiously, you chariots! Let the warriors go out: Cush and Put, who carry the shield, and the Ludim, who draw the bow.[^8]
עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת׃

That day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies,[^9] a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword will devour and be satisfied, and drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord GOD of Armies holds a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the Euphrates River.

וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֙רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל־נְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃
Go up to Gilead and get balm,[^10] virgin Daughter Egypt! In vain you have used many medicines;[^11] there is no healing for you.
עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ *הרביתי **הִרְבֵּ֣ית רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ׃
The nations have heard of your shame; your cry fills the earth. For warrior has stumbled against warrior; both have fallen together.
שָׁמְע֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ קְלוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְצִוְחָתֵ֖ךְ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־גִבּ֤וֹר בְּגִבּוֹר֙ כָּשָׁ֔לוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו נָפְל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃ פ
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:[^12]
הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
Declare it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it in Memphis and in Tahpanhes.[^13] Say: Take your stand and get ready, for the sword devours those around you.
הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ׃
Why has your mighty one been swept away?[^14] He did not stand, because the LORD drove him down.
מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ׃
He made many stumble; they fell, each against the other. They said, "Get up, let us go back to our own people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor."[^15]
הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם־נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה ׀ וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל־עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל־אֶ֙רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה׃
There they cried out, "Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by."[^16]
קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד׃
As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, one will come like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea.[^17]
חַי־אָ֙נִי֙ נְאֻם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא׃
Pack your bags for exile, you who live there, Daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a desolation, burned[^18] and empty of inhabitants.
כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ ס
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly[^19] from the north has come, has come!
עֶגְלָ֥ה יְפֵֽה־פִיָּ֖ה מִצְרָ֑יִם קֶ֥רֶץ מִצָּפ֖וֹן בָּ֥א בָֽא׃

Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves. They too have turned and fled together; they did not stand. For the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
גַּם־שְׂכִרֶ֤יהָ בְקִרְבָּהּ֙ כְּעֶגְלֵ֣י מַרְבֵּ֔ק כִּֽי־גַם־הֵ֧מָּה הִפְנ֛וּ נָ֥סוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו לֹ֣א עָמָ֑דוּ כִּ֣י י֥וֹם אֵידָ֛ם בָּ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃
Her sound is like a snake slithering away,[^20] for they march on in force; they come against her with axes, like those who cut down trees.
קוֹלָ֖הּ כַּנָּחָ֣שׁ יֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־בְחַ֣יִל יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְקַרְדֻּמּוֹת֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔הּ כְּחֹטְבֵ֖י עֵצִֽים׃
They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it cannot be searched through,[^21] for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
כָּרְת֤וּ יַעְרָהּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י לֹ֣א יֵֽחָקֵ֑ר כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ מֵֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מִסְפָּֽר׃
Daughter Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of the people of the north.
הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת־מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד עַם־צָפֽוֹן׃
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish Amon of Thebes,[^22] and Pharaoh and Egypt, her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and those who trust in him.
אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י פוֹקֵד֙ אֶל־אָמ֣וֹן מִנֹּ֔א וְעַל־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְעַל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ וְעַל־מְלָכֶ֑יהָ וְעַ֨ל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְעַ֥ל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

I will give them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. But afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.
וּנְתַתִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֔ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַד־עֲבָדָ֑יו וְאַחֲרֵי[t] כֵ֛ן תִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן כִּֽימֵי־קֶ֖דֶם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

As for you, do not be afraid, Jacob my servant; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I am going to save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace and secure, and no one will make him afraid.[^23]

וְ֠אַתָּה אַל־תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲק֛וֹב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ ס

As for you, do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, declares the LORD, for I am with you. I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you with justice,[^24] and I will by no means leave you unpunished.

אַ֠תָּה אַל־תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִתְּךָ֖ אָ֑נִי כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם ׀ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣יךָ שָׁ֗מָּה וְאֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹא־אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֙יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Verse 1 is the heading of the oracles against the nations in chapters 46–51. In the Septuagint they come after 25:13 (see the note there), and in a different order: Elam (49:34–39), Egypt (46), Babylon (50–51), the Philistines (47), Edom (49:7–22), Ammon (49:1–6), Kedar (49:28–33), Damascus (49:23–27) and Moab (48).
n.3: In 605 BC. Carchemish was on the upper Euphrates, on the present border of Turkey and Syria. Four years earlier Neco had killed King Josiah at Megiddo (2 Kings 23:29).
n.4: Hebrew *magen*, a small round shield, and *tsinnah*, a large shield that covered the whole body.
n.5: Or "mount the stallions".
n.6: Hebrew *magor missaviv*: see 6:25.
n.7: Hebrew *ye'or*, the Nile, which rose in flood each year. Also in verse 8.
n.8: Literally "who grasp, who bend the bow". Cush was the land south of Egypt, and Put was probably Libya. The Ludim may be Lydians from Asia Minor. All served in Egypt's army.
n.9: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH tseva'ot*, "my Lord YHWH of Armies". *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *The LORD of Armies* is also in verses 18 and 25.
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "I have used many medicines" but read "you have used many medicines". The written form may be an old spelling of "you have used" (compare 2:20, 33).
n.12: Compare 43:8–13.
n.14: Hebrew *abbirekha*, "your mighty one", a word also used of a bull. The Septuagint divides the letters differently and reads "Why has Apis fled? Your chosen calf did not stand." Apis was the sacred bull worshiped at Memphis.
n.15: Or "the cruel sword". Hebrew *ha-yonah*, perhaps "the oppressor" (25:38; 50:16).
n.16: Or, with the same consonants, "Call Pharaoh king of Egypt by the name 'Big Noise, who let the appointed time pass by'." The Hebrew *sha'on*, "noise, uproar", may mock a royal title.
n.17: Mount Tabor rises alone above the plain of Jezreel, and Mount Carmel above the Mediterranean coast. The one who comes is the king of Babylon.
n.18: Or "laid waste".
n.19: Hebrew *qerets*, a rare word, perhaps "gadfly" or "horsefly".
n.20: Literally "Her sound goes like a snake". Egypt hisses and slips away as the enemy advances.
n.22: Amon was the chief god of Thebes (Hebrew *No*), the great city of Upper Egypt.

v: The word of the LORD[^1] that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.[^2]
אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת־עַזָּֽה׃ ס

This is what the LORD says: Look, waters are rising from the north; they will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and everything in it, the city and those who live in it. People will cry out, and all who live in the land will wail.

כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנֵּה־מַ֜יִם עֹלִ֤ים מִצָּפוֹן֙ וְהָיוּ֙ לְנַ֣חַל שׁוֹטֵ֔ף וְיִ[t]שְׁטְפוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֔הּ עִ֖יר וְיֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ וְזָֽעֲקוּ֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְהֵילִ֕ל כֹּ֖ל יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
At the sound of the stamping hooves of his stallions, at the rumble of his chariots and the clatter of their wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children, because their hands hang limp.[^3]
מִקּ֗וֹל שַֽׁעֲטַת֙ פַּרְס֣וֹת אַבִּירָ֔יו מֵרַ֣עַשׁ לְרִכְבּ֔וֹ הֲמ֖וֹן גַּלְגִּלָּ֑יו לֹֽא־הִפְנ֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ אֶל־בָּנִ֔ים מֵֽרִפְי֖וֹן יָדָֽיִם׃

For the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper who survives. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.[^4]
עַל־הַיּ֗וֹם הַבָּא֙ לִשְׁד֣וֹד אֶת־כָּל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהַכְרִ֤ית לְצֹר֙ וּלְצִיד֔וֹן כֹּ֖ל שָׂרִ֣יד עֹזֵ֑ר כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שְׁאֵרִ֖ית אִ֥י כַפְתּֽוֹר׃
Baldness has come upon Gaza;[^5] Ashkelon is silenced. Remnant of their valley,[^6] how long will you gash yourself?
בָּ֤אָה קָרְחָה֙ אֶל־עַזָּ֔ה נִדְמְתָ֥ה אַשְׁקְל֖וֹן שְׁאֵרִ֣ית עִמְקָ֑ם עַד־מָתַ֖י תִּתְגּוֹדָֽדִי׃ ס
Ah,[^7] sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Go back into your sheath; rest and be still.
ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַד־אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי הֵאָֽסְפִי֙ אַל־תַּעְרֵ֔ךְ הֵרָגְעִ֖י וָדֹֽמִּי׃
How can it be quiet,[^8] when the LORD has given it a command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast, there he has appointed it.
אֵ֣יךְ תִּשְׁקֹ֔טִי וַֽיהוָ֖ה צִוָּה־לָ֑הּ אֶֽל־אַשְׁקְל֛וֹן וְאֶל־ח֥וֹף הַיָּ֖ם שָׁ֥ם יְעָדָֽהּ׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The occasion is not known. Gaza, Ashkelon and the other Philistine cities lay on the coastal plain southwest of Judah.
n.3: Literally "because of the slackness of hands".
n.4: Caphtor is probably Crete, from which the Philistines had come (Amos 9:7; Deuteronomy 2:23). Hebrew *i*, "coastland, island".
n.5: The head was shaved in mourning (16:6; 48:37).
n.6: Hebrew *imqam*, "their valley", perhaps the coastal plain. The Septuagint reads "the remnant of the Anakim", the giants of old who had lived in the Philistine cities (Joshua 11:22).
n.7: Hebrew *hoy*, translated "Woe to" in 22:13, here a cry of lament.
n.8: Literally "How can you be quiet".

v: Concerning Moab. This is what the LORD of Armies,[^1] the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo,[^2] for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold[^3] is put to shame and shattered.
לְמוֹאָ֡ב כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ה֤וֹי אֶל־נְבוֹ֙ כִּ֣י שֻׁדָּ֔דָה הֹבִ֥ישָׁה נִלְכְּדָ֖ה קִרְיָתָ֑יִם הֹבִ֥ישָׁה הַמִּשְׂגָּ֖ב וָחָֽתָּה׃
Moab's renown is no more. In Heshbon they have planned disaster against her:[^4] "Come, let us cut her off from being a nation." You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.
אֵ֣ין עוֹד֮ תְּהִלַּ֣ת מוֹאָב֒ בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן חָשְׁב֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ רָעָ֔ה לְכ֖וּ וְנַכְרִיתֶ֣נָּה מִגּ֑וֹי גַּם־מַדְמֵ֣ן תִּדֹּ֔מִּי אַחֲרַ֖יִךְ תֵּ֥לֶךְ חָֽרֶב׃
Listen! A cry from Horonaim: "Devastation and great destruction!"
ק֥וֹל צְעָקָ֖ה מֵחֹֽרוֹנָ֑יִם שֹׁ֖ד וָשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃
Moab is shattered; her little ones raise a cry.[^5]
נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה מוֹאָ֑ב הִשְׁמִ֥יעוּ זְּעָקָ֖ה *צעוריה **צְעִירֶֽיהָ׃
For on the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping bitterly;[^6] for on the descent to Horonaim they have heard the anguished cry of destruction.
כִּ֚י מַעֲלֵ֣ה *הלחות **הַלּוּחִ֔ית בִּבְכִ֖י יַֽעֲלֶה־בֶּ֑כִי כִּ֚י בְּמוֹרַ֣ד חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם צָרֵ֥י צַֽעֲקַת־שֶׁ֖בֶר שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃
Flee! Save your lives! Be like a juniper[^7] in the wilderness.
נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וְתִֽהְיֶ֔ינָה כַּעֲרוֹעֵ֖ר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh[^8] will go into exile, together with his priests and his officials.
כִּ֠י יַ֣עַן בִּטְחֵ֤ךְ בְּמַעֲשַׂ֙יִךְ֙ וּבְא֣וֹצְרוֹתַ֔יִךְ גַּם־אַ֖תְּ תִּלָּכֵ֑דִי וְיָצָ֤א *כמיש **כְמוֹשׁ֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֔ה כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו *יחד **יַחְדָּֽיו׃
The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will perish, and the plateau[^9] will be destroyed, as the LORD has said.
וְיָבֹ֨א שֹׁדֵ֜ד אֶל־כָּל־עִ֗יר וְעִיר֙ לֹ֣א תִמָּלֵ֔ט וְאָבַ֥ד הָעֵ֖מֶק וְנִשְׁמַ֣ד הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
Give wings to Moab,[^10] for she will surely fly away. Her cities will become a desolation, with no one living in them.
תְּנוּ־צִ֣יץ לְמוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י נָצֹ֖א תֵּצֵ֑א וְעָרֶ֙יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּהֵֽן׃
Cursed is anyone who does the work of the LORD carelessly; cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from bloodshed!
אָר֗וּר עֹשֶׂ֛ה מְלֶ֥אכֶת יְהוָ֖ה רְמִיָּ֑ה וְאָר֕וּר מֹנֵ֥עַ חַרְבּ֖וֹ מִדָּֽם׃

Moab has been at ease from his youth, settled like wine on its dregs. He has not been poured from jar to jar; he has not gone into exile. So his flavor has stayed in him, and his aroma has not changed.[^11]
שַׁאֲנַ֨ן מוֹאָ֜ב מִנְּעוּרָ֗יו וְשֹׁקֵ֥ט הוּא֙ אֶל־שְׁמָרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־הוּרַ֤ק מִכְּלִי֙ אֶל־כֶּ֔לִי וּבַגּוֹלָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ עַל־כֵּ֗ן עָמַ֤ד טַעְמוֹ֙ בּ֔וֹ וְרֵיח֖וֹ לֹ֥א נָמָֽר׃ ס
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send him pourers,[^12] and they will pour him out. They will empty his jars and smash his jugs.
לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּ֖ה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־ל֥וֹ צֹעִ֖ים וְצֵעֻ֑הוּ וְכֵלָ֣יו יָרִ֔יקוּ וְנִבְלֵיהֶ֖ם יְנַפֵּֽצוּ׃
Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which they trusted.[^13]
וּבֹ֥שׁ מוֹאָ֖ב מִכְּמ֑וֹשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר־בֹּ֙שׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ית אֵ֖ל מִבְטֶחָֽם׃
How can you say, "We are warriors, mighty men for battle"?
אֵ֚יךְ תֹּֽאמְר֔וּ גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
Moab is devastated, and his cities have been invaded;[^14] the best of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
שֻׁדַּ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ וְעָרֶ֣יהָ עָלָ֔ה וּמִבְחַ֥ר בַּֽחוּרָ֖יו יָרְד֣וּ לַטָּ֑בַח נְאֻ֨ם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃
Moab's calamity is near at hand; his disaster is coming quickly.
קָר֥וֹב אֵיד־מוֹאָ֖ב לָב֑וֹא וְרָ֣עָת֔וֹ מִהֲרָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
Mourn for him, all you who are around him, all who know his name. Say, "How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!"
נֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ כָּל־סְבִיבָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל יֹדְעֵ֣י שְׁמ֑וֹ אִמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֤ה נִשְׁבַּר֙ מַטֵּה־עֹ֔ז מַקֵּ֖ל תִּפְאָרָֽה׃
Come down from your glory and sit on the parched ground, you who live there, Daughter Dibon,[^15] for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
רְדִ֤י מִכָּבוֹד֙ *ישבי **וּשְׁבִ֣י בַצָּמָ֔א יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־דִּיב֑וֹן כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ עָ֣לָה בָ֔ךְ שִׁחֵ֖ת מִבְצָרָֽיִךְ׃
Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask the man who flees and the woman who escapes; say, "What has happened?"
אֶל־דֶּ֛רֶךְ עִמְדִ֥י וְצַפִּ֖י יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת עֲרוֹעֵ֑ר שַׁאֲלִי־נָ֣ס וְנִמְלָ֔טָה אִמְרִ֖י מַה־נִּֽהְיָֽתָה׃
Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Proclaim by the Arnon[^16] that Moab is devastated.
הֹבִ֥ישׁ מוֹאָ֛ב כִּֽי־חַ֖תָּה *הילילי **הֵילִ֣ילוּ ׀ *וזעקי **וּֽזְעָ֑קוּ הַגִּ֣ידוּ בְאַרְנ֔וֹן כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מוֹאָֽב׃
Judgment has come to the land of the plateau: to Holon, to Jahzah and to Mephaath,
וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל־חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל־יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל־*מופעת **מֵיפָֽעַת׃
to Dibon, to Nebo and to Beth-diblathaim,
וְעַל־דִּיב֣וֹן וְעַל־נְב֔וֹ וְעַל־בֵּ֖ית דִּבְלָתָֽיִם׃
to Kiriathaim, to Beth-gamul and to Beth-meon,
וְעַ֧ל קִרְיָתַ֛יִם וְעַל־בֵּ֥ית גָּמ֖וּל וְעַל־בֵּ֥ית מְעֽוֹן׃
to Kerioth and to Bozrah,[^17] and to all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
וְעַל־קְרִיּ֖וֹת וְעַל־בָּצְרָ֑ה וְעַ֗ל כָּל־עָרֵי֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב הָרְחֹק֖וֹת וְהַקְּרֹבֽוֹת׃
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,[^18] declares the LORD.
נִגְדְּעָה֙ קֶ֣רֶן מוֹאָ֔ב וּזְרֹע֖וֹ נִשְׁבָּ֑רָה נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
Make him drunk, for he has made himself great against the LORD. Let Moab wallow in his vomit, and let him also become a laughingstock.
הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ כִּ֥י עַל־יְהוָ֖ה הִגְדִּ֑יל וְסָפַ֤ק מוֹאָב֙ בְּקִיא֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לִשְׂחֹ֖ק גַּם־הֽוּא׃
Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he caught among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you shook your head?
וְאִ֣ם ׀ ל֣וֹא הַשְּׂחֹ֗ק הָיָ֤ה לְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־בְּגַנָּבִ֖ים *נמצאה **נִמְצָ֑א כִּֽי־מִדֵּ֧י דְבָרֶ֛יךָ בּ֖וֹ תִּתְנוֹדָֽד׃
Leave the cities and live among the rocks, you who live in Moab! Be like a dove that nests on the sides of the mouth of a gorge.
עִזְב֤וּ עָרִים֙ וְשִׁכְנ֣וּ בַסֶּ֔לַע יֹשְׁבֵ֖י מוֹאָ֑ב וִֽהְי֣וּ כְיוֹנָ֔ה תְּקַנֵּ֖ן בְּעֶבְרֵ֥י פִי־פָֽחַת׃
We have heard of the pride of Moab, how very proud he is: his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance and his haughty heart.[^19]
שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּאֶ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד גָּבְה֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְגַאֲוָת֖וֹ וְרֻ֥ם לִבּֽוֹ׃
I know his insolence, declares the LORD, but it is empty; his boasts accomplish nothing.[^20]
אֲנִ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה עֶבְרָת֖וֹ וְלֹא־כֵ֑ן בַּדָּ֖יו לֹא־כֵ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃
Therefore I wail for Moab; for all Moab I cry out; for the men of Kir-heres[^21] one moans.
עַל־כֵּן֙ עַל־מוֹאָ֣ב אֲיֵלִ֔יל וּלְמוֹאָ֥ב כֻּלֹּ֖ה אֶזְעָ֑ק אֶל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י קִֽיר־חֶ֖רֶשׂ יֶהְגֶּֽה׃

More than the weeping for Jazer I weep for you, vine of Sibmah! Your tendrils crossed over the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer.[^22] On your summer fruit and on your grape harvest the destroyer has fallen.
מִבְּכִ֨י יַעְזֵ֤ר אֶבְכֶּה־לָּךְ֙ הַגֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֙יִךְ֙ עָ֣בְרוּ יָ֔ם עַ֛ד יָ֥ם יַעְזֵ֖ר נָגָ֑עוּ עַל־קֵיצֵ֥ךְ וְעַל־בְּצִירֵ֖ךְ שֹׁדֵ֥ד נָפָֽל׃

Joy and gladness have been taken away from the orchard[^23] and from the land of Moab. I have stopped the wine from the winepresses; no one treads them with shouts of joy. The shouting is no shout of joy.[^24]
וְנֶאֶסְפָ֨ה שִׂמְחָ֥ה וָגִ֛יל מִכַּרְמֶ֖ל וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב וְיַ֙יִן֙ מִיקָבִ֣ים הִשְׁבַּ֔תִּי לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֣ךְ הֵידָ֔ד הֵידָ֖ד לֹ֥א הֵידָֽד׃
From the outcry at Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz they raise their voice, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah.[^25] For even the waters of Nimrim have become desolate.
מִזַּעֲקַ֨ת חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן עַד־אֶלְעָלֵ֗ה עַד־יַ֙הַץ֙ נָתְנ֣וּ קוֹלָ֔ם מִצֹּ֙עַר֙ עַד־חֹ֣רֹנַ֔יִם עֶגְלַ֖ת שְׁלִֽשִׁיָּ֑ה כִּ֚י גַּם־מֵ֣י נִמְרִ֔ים לִמְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יִהְיֽוּ׃
I will put an end in Moab, declares the LORD, to those who offer sacrifices on the high place and burn incense[^26] to their gods.
וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֥י לְמוֹאָ֖ב נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה מַעֲלֶ֣ה בָמָ֔ה וּמַקְטִ֖יר לֵאלֹהָֽיו׃
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like a flute; my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-heres. Therefore the wealth they gained has perished.[^27]
עַל־כֵּ֞ן לִבִּ֤י לְמוֹאָב֙ כַּחֲלִלִ֣ים יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְלִבִּי֙ אֶל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י קִֽיר־חֶ֔רֶשׂ כַּחֲלִילִ֖ים יֶהֱמֶ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֛ן יִתְרַ֥ת עָשָׂ֖ה אָבָֽדוּ׃
For every head is shaved bald and every beard cut off; on every hand are gashes, and around the waist is sackcloth.
כִּ֤י כָל־רֹאשׁ֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְכָל־זָקָ֖ן גְּרֻעָ֑ה עַ֤ל כָּל־יָדַ֙יִם֙ גְּדֻדֹ֔ת וְעַל־מָתְנַ֖יִם שָֽׂק׃
On all the roofs of Moab and in its squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have broken Moab like a jar that no one wants, declares the LORD.
עַ֣ל כָּל־גַּגּ֥וֹת מוֹאָ֛ב וּבִרְחֹבֹתֶ֖יהָ כֻּלֹּ֣ה מִסְפֵּ֑ד כִּֽי־שָׁבַ֣רְתִּי אֶת־מוֹאָ֗ב כִּכְלִ֛י אֵֽין־חֵ֥פֶץ בּ֖וֹ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
How it is shattered! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and an object of terror to all those around him.
אֵ֥יךְ חַ֙תָּה֙ הֵילִ֔ילוּ אֵ֛יךְ הִפְנָה־עֹ֥רֶף מוֹאָ֖ב בּ֑וֹשׁ וְהָיָ֥ה מוֹאָ֛ב לִשְׂחֹ֥ק וְלִמְחִתָּ֖ה לְכָל־סְבִיבָֽיו׃ ס
For this is what the LORD says: Look, one swoops down like an eagle and spreads his wings over Moab.[^28]
כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה כַנֶּ֖שֶׁר יִדְאֶ֑ה וּפָרַ֥שׂ כְּנָפָ֖יו אֶל־מוֹאָֽב׃
Kerioth is captured,[^29] and the strongholds are seized. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
נִלְכְּדָה֙ הַקְּרִיּ֔וֹת וְהַמְּצָד֖וֹת נִתְפָּ֑שָׂה וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה׃
Moab will be destroyed and be a people no more, because he made himself great against the LORD.
וְנִשְׁמַ֥ד מוֹאָ֖ב מֵעָ֑ם כִּ֥י עַל־יְהוָ֖ה הִגְדִּֽיל׃
Terror, pit and trap are before you, you who live in Moab, declares the LORD.[^30]
פַּ֥חַד וָפַ֖חַת וָפָ֑ח עָלֶ֛יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב מוֹאָ֖ב נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

Whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For I will bring upon her, upon Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
*הניס **הַנָּ֞ס מִפְּנֵ֤י הַפַּ֙חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל־הַפַּ֔חַת וְהָֽעֹלֶה֙ מִן־הַפַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּפָּ֑ח כִּֽי־אָבִ֨יא אֵלֶ֧יהָ אֶל־מוֹאָ֛ב שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand without strength. For fire has gone out from Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon.[^31] It has devoured the forehead of Moab and the skulls of the boasters.[^32]
בְּצֵ֥ל חֶשְׁבּ֛וֹן עָמְד֖וּ מִכֹּ֣חַ נָסִ֑ים כִּֽי־אֵ֞שׁ יָצָ֣א מֵחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן וְלֶֽהָבָה֙ מִבֵּ֣ין סִיח֔וֹן וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ פְּאַ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב וְקָדְקֹ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י שָׁאֽוֹן׃
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken into captivity, and your daughters into exile.
אוֹי־לְךָ֣ מוֹאָ֔ב אָבַ֖ד עַם־כְּמ֑וֹשׁ כִּֽי־לֻקְּח֤וּ בָנֶ֙יךָ֙ בַּשֶּׁ֔בִי וּבְנֹתֶ֖יךָ בַּשִּׁבְיָֽה׃
Yet I will restore the fortunes[^33] of Moab in the days to come,[^34] declares the LORD. Thus far the judgment on Moab.
וְשַׁבְתִּ֧י שְׁבוּת־מוֹאָ֛ב בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה עַד־הֵ֖נָּה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט מוֹאָֽב׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 15. Much of this chapter has lines in common with Isaiah 15–16.
n.2: The places named in this chapter are towns of Moab, east of the Dead Sea. Nebo is the town, not the mountain (Numbers 32:38).
n.3: Hebrew *ha-misgav*, "the high stronghold", perhaps a place name, Misgab.
n.4: Two wordplays: *Cheshbon*, "Heshbon", and *chashvu*, "they have planned"; *Madmen* and *tiddommi*, "you will be silenced".
n.5: The Septuagint reads "they raise a cry to Zoar" (compare Isaiah 15:5).
n.6: Literally "with weeping goes up weeping". Compare Isaiah 15:5.
n.7: Hebrew *aro'er*, perhaps a desert shrub (compare 17:6), or the town of Aroer (verse 19).
n.8: The god of Moab (Numbers 21:29; 1 Kings 11:7).
n.9: Hebrew *ha-mishor*, the high tableland of Moab. Also in verse 21.
n.10: The meaning of the Hebrew *tsits* is uncertain here. It may mean "wings", "a flower" or "salt".
n.11: Wine was left to settle on its sediment and then poured off into other jars to clear it.
n.12: Hebrew *tso'im*, "those who tip", men who tilt jars to pour them out.
n.13: Bethel was where Jeroboam set up a golden calf for Israel to worship (1 Kings 12:28–29). Or the god Bethel, who was worshiped in the region.
n.14: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "and her cities he has gone up".
n.15: Dibon was a chief city of Moab, north of the Arnon.
n.16: The deep gorge of the Arnon cuts through Moab to the Dead Sea.
n.17: A town in Moab, not the Bozrah of Edom (49:13).
n.18: Pictures of strength.
n.19: Verses 29–38 have many lines in common with Isaiah 16:6–11 and 15:2–7.
n.20: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "and not right; his empty talk, not right they have done".
n.21: Called Kir-hareseth in Isaiah 16:7, a chief fortress of Moab. Also in verse 36.
n.22: Isaiah 16:8 reads "they reached as far as Jazer". The *sea* is probably the Dead Sea.
n.24: Literally "the shout is not a shout". The cry of the grape treaders has become the battle cry of the enemy (25:30; 51:14).
n.26: Or "burn offerings". The Hebrew verb *qatar* means to make something go up in smoke.
n.27: Literally "the abundance he made has perished" (Isaiah 15:7). Flutes were played at funerals.
n.28: Verses 40–41 are nearly the same as 49:22, which is said of Edom.
n.29: Or "The towns are captured". Hebrew *qeriyyot*, "towns", is also the name of Kerioth (verse 24).
n.30: A wordplay: *pachad*, "terror", *pachat*, "pit", and *pach*, "trap". Verses 43–44 are nearly the same as Isaiah 24:17–18.
n.31: Verses 45–46 draw on the ancient song in Numbers 21:28–29 and on Numbers 24:17. Sihon was the Amorite king whose capital was Heshbon (Numbers 21:26).
n.32: Literally "the sons of tumult". Numbers 24:17 has "the sons of Sheth".
n.33: Literally "turn the turning", an idiom for restoring what was lost. Or "bring back the captives".
n.34: Literally "in the latter end of the days".

v: Concerning the Ammonites. This is what the LORD[^1] says: Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom[^2] taken possession of Gad, and why do his people live in its cities?
לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲבָנִ֥ים אֵין֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־יוֹרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ מַדּ֗וּעַ יָרַ֤שׁ מַלְכָּם֙ אֶת־גָּ֔ד וְעַמּ֖וֹ בְּעָרָ֥יו יָשָֽׁב׃

Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make the battle cry heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites.[^3] It will become a desolate mound, and its villages[^4] will be burned with fire. Then Israel will take possession of those who took possession of him, says the LORD.

לָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּה֩ יָמִ֨ים בָּאִ֜ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה וְ֠הִשְׁמַעְתִּי אֶל־רַבַּ֨ת בְּנֵי־עַמּ֜וֹן תְּרוּעַ֣ת מִלְחָמָ֗ה וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְתֵ֣ל שְׁמָמָ֔ה וּבְנֹתֶ֖יהָ בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּצַּ֑תְנָה וְיָרַ֧שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־יֹרְשָׁ֖יו אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated![^5] Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth among the walls,[^6] for Milcom will go into exile, together with his priests and his officials.

הֵילִ֨ילִי חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן כִּ֣י שֻׁדְּדָה־עַ֗י צְעַקְנָה֮ בְּנ֣וֹת רַבָּה֒ חֲגֹ֣רְנָה שַׂקִּ֔ים סְפֹ֕דְנָה וְהִתְשׁוֹטַ֖טְנָה בַּגְּדֵר֑וֹת כִּ֤י מַלְכָּם֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֣ה יֵלֵ֔ךְ כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו יַחְדָּֽיו׃
Why do you boast of your valleys, your valley overflowing,[^7] faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, "Who will come against me?"
מַה־תִּתְהַֽלְלִי֙ בָּֽעֲמָקִ֔ים זָ֣ב עִמְקֵ֔ךְ הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה הַבֹּֽטְחָה֙ בְּאֹ֣צְרֹתֶ֔יהָ מִ֖י יָב֥וֹא אֵלָֽי׃
I am going to bring terror on you, declares the Lord GOD of Armies,[^8] from all who are around you. You will be driven away, each one headlong, with no one to gather the fugitives.
הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא עָלַ֜יִךְ פַּ֗חַד נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת מִכָּל־סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד׃
But afterward I will restore the fortunes[^9] of the Ammonites, declares the LORD.
וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־שְׁב֥וּת בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Concerning Edom. This is what the LORD of Armies says: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman?[^10] Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom gone bad?
לֶאֱד֗וֹם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַאֵ֥ין ע֛וֹד חָכְמָ֖ה בְּתֵימָ֑ן אָבְדָ֤ה עֵצָה֙ מִבָּנִ֔ים נִסְרְחָ֖ה חָכְמָתָֽם׃
Flee, turn back, hide deep down,[^11] you who live in Dedan! For I will bring disaster on Esau, the time when I punish him.
נֻ֤סוּ הָפְנוּ֙ הֶעְמִ֣יקוּ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֖י דְּדָ֑ן כִּ֣י אֵ֥יד עֵשָׂ֛ו הֵבֵ֥אתִי עָלָ֖יו עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיו׃
If grape pickers came to you, they would leave no gleanings. If thieves came by night, they would destroy all they wanted.[^12]
אִם־בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ לֹ֥א יַשְׁאִ֖רוּ עֽוֹלֵל֑וֹת אִם־גַּנָּבִ֥ים בַּלַּ֖יְלָה הִשְׁחִ֥יתוּ דַיָּֽם׃
But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he cannot hide himself. His offspring are destroyed, his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.
כִּֽי־אֲנִ֞י חָשַׂ֣פְתִּי אֶת־עֵשָׂ֗ו גִּלֵּ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־מִסְתָּרָ֔יו וְנֶחְבָּ֖ה לֹ֣א יוּכָ֑ל שֻׁדַּ֥ד זַרְע֛וֹ וְאֶחָ֥יו וּשְׁכֵנָ֖יו וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
עָזְבָ֥ה יְתֹמֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֣י אֲחַיֶּ֑ה וְאַלְמְנֹתֶ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י תִּבְטָֽחוּ׃ ס
For this is what the LORD says: If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it,[^13] will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you will surely drink it.
כִּי־כֹ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִ֠נֵּה אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֨ין מִשְׁפָּטָ֜ם לִשְׁתּ֤וֹת הַכּוֹס֙ שָׁת֣וֹ יִשְׁתּ֔וּ וְאַתָּ֣ה ה֔וּא נָקֹ֖ה תִּנָּקֶ֑ה לֹ֣א תִנָּקֶ֔ה כִּ֥י שָׁתֹ֖ה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃
For I have sworn by myself, declares the LORD, that Bozrah[^14] will become a horror, a disgrace, a ruin and a curse, and all her cities will be ruins forever.
כִּ֣י בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֙עְתִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־לְשַׁמָּ֧ה לְחֶרְפָּ֛ה לְחֹ֥רֶב וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה בָצְרָ֑ה וְכָל־עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃
I have heard a report from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Gather together and come against her; rise up for battle!"
שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וְצִ֖יר בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שָׁל֑וּחַ הִֽתְקַבְּצוּ֙ וּבֹ֣אוּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְק֖וּמוּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
For look, I will make you small among the nations, despised among human beings.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֖וּי בָּאָדָֽם׃

The terror you inspire[^15] and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock,[^16] who hold the height of the hill. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
תִּֽפְלַצְתְּךָ֞ הִשִּׁ֤יא אֹתָךְ֙ זְד֣וֹן לִבֶּ֔ךָ שֹֽׁכְנִי֙ בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֔לַע תֹּפְשִׂ֖י מְר֣וֹם גִּבְעָ֑ה כִּֽי־תַגְבִּ֤יהַ כַּנֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ קִנֶּ֔ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אֽוֹרִידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Edom will become a horror; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.
וְהָיְתָ֥ה אֱד֖וֹם לְשַׁמָּ֑ה כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכּוֹתֶֽהָ׃
As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors were overthrown, says the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will stay in it.[^17]
כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת סְדֹ֧ם וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וּשְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃

Look, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan[^18] to a pasture that is always green,[^19] I will suddenly chase them from it, and I will appoint over it whoever is chosen.[^20] For who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־אַרְגִּ֤יעָה אֲרִיצֶ֙נּוּ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֙וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יֹעִידֶ֔נִּי וּמִי־זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃ ס

Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Edom, and the purposes he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־אֱד֔וֹם וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵימָ֑ן אִם־לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נְוֵהֶֽם׃
At the sound of their fall the earth quakes; their cry is heard at the Red Sea.[^21]
מִקּ֣וֹל נִפְלָ֔ם רָעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ צְעָקָ֕ה בְּיַם־ס֖וּף נִשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלָֽהּ׃
Look, like an eagle he will rise and swoop down and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
הִנֵּ֤ה כַנֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה וְיִדְאֶ֔ה וְיִפְרֹ֥שׂ כְּנָפָ֖יו עַל־בָּצְרָ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י אֱדוֹם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה׃ ס
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad[^22] are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt in fear; there is anxiety like the sea,[^23] which cannot be calm.
לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק בּ֤וֹשָֽׁה חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד כִּי־שְׁמֻעָ֥ה רָעָ֛ה שָׁמְע֖וּ נָמֹ֑גוּ בַּיָּ֣ם דְּאָגָ֔ה הַשְׁקֵ֖ט לֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃
Damascus has grown weak; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pangs have gripped her like a woman in labor.
רָפְתָ֥ה דַמֶּ֛שֶׂק הִפְנְתָ֥ה לָנ֖וּס וְרֶ֣טֶט ׀ הֶחֱזִ֑יקָה צָרָ֧ה וַחֲבָלִ֛ים אֲחָזַ֖תָּה כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃
How is it that the city of praise has not been abandoned, the town of my joy?[^24]
אֵ֥יךְ לֹֽא־עֻזְּבָ֖ה עִ֣יר *תהלה **תְּהִלָּ֑ת קִרְיַ֖ת מְשׂוֹשִֽׂי׃
Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD of Armies.[^25]
לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה יִדַּ֙מּוּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
I will set fire to the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.[^26]
וְהִצַּ֥תִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת בֶּן־הֲדָֽד׃ ס
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down.[^27] This is what the LORD says: Rise up, go up against Kedar, and destroy the people of the east.
לְקֵדָ֣ר ׀ וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ *נבוכדראצור **נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ אֶל־קֵדָ֔ר וְשָׁדְד֖וּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
Their tents and their flocks will be taken, their tent curtains and all their goods; their camels will be carried off from them. People will shout to them, "Terror on every side!"
אָהֳלֵיהֶ֤ם וְצֹאנָם֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ יְרִיעוֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְכָל־כְּלֵיהֶ֛ם וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם יִשְׂא֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְקָרְא֧וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם מָג֖וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃
Flee, wander far away, hide deep down, you who live in Hazor, declares the LORD. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you; he has formed a purpose against you.[^28]
נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָשֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָעַ֨ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ עֵצָ֔ה וְחָשַׁ֥ב *עליהם **עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַחֲשָׁבָֽה׃
Rise up, go up against a nation at ease, that lives in security, declares the LORD, that has no gates or bars; they live alone.
ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ אֶל־גּ֥וֹי שְׁלֵ֛יו יוֹשֵׁ֥ב לָבֶ֖טַח נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־דְלָתַ֧יִם וְלֹֽא־בְרִ֛יחַ ל֖וֹ בָּדָ֥ד יִשְׁכֹּֽנוּ׃

Their camels will become plunder, and their great herds spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who clip the hair at their temples,[^29] and I will bring disaster on them from every side, declares the LORD.
וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם לָבַ֗ז וַהֲמ֤וֹן מִקְנֵיהֶם֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל וְזֵרִתִ֥ים לְכָל־ר֖וּחַ קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֑ה וּמִכָּל־עֲבָרָ֛יו אָבִ֥יא אֶת־אֵידָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there; no human being will stay in it.
וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃ ס
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam,[^30] at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־עֵילָ֑ם בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might.[^31]
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י שֹׁבֵ֖ר אֶת־קֶ֣שֶׁת עֵילָ֑ם רֵאשִׁ֖ית גְּבוּרָתָֽם׃
I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam[^32] will not come.
וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י אֶל־עֵילָ֜ם אַרְבַּ֣ע רוּח֗וֹת מֵֽאַרְבַּע֙ קְצ֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְזֵ֣רִתִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל הָרֻח֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה הַגּ֔וֹי אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא שָׁ֖ם נִדְּחֵ֥י *עולם **עֵילָֽם׃

I will shatter Elam before their enemies, before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster on them, my fierce anger, declares the LORD. I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.

וְהַחְתַּתִּ֣י אֶת־עֵ֠ילָם לִפְנֵ֨י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֜ם וְלִפְנֵ֣י ׀ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֧ם ׀ רָעָ֛ה אֶת־חֲר֥וֹן אַפִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy from there its king and officials, declares the LORD.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י כִסְאִ֖י בְּעֵילָ֑ם וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֛ם מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
But in the days to come[^33] I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים *אשוב **אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־*שבית **שְׁב֥וּת עֵילָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The Hebrew is pointed *malkam*, "their king". The same consonants can be read *Milkom*, Milcom, the god of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5, 33), as the Septuagint reads. Also in verse 3, where Milcom goes into exile with his priests, as Chemosh does in 48:7.
n.3: The Ammonite capital, modern Amman.
n.4: Literally "its daughters".
n.5: This Ai, in Ammon, is not the town near Bethel. Heshbon lay near the border of Ammon and Moab (48:2).
n.6: Hebrew *gederot*, "walls" or "sheepfolds". The meaning of the line is uncertain.
n.7: Literally "your valley flows".
n.8: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH tseva'ot*, "my Lord YHWH of Armies". *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *The LORD of Armies* is also in verses 7, 26 and 35.
n.9: Literally "turn the turning", an idiom for restoring what was lost. Or "bring back the captives". Also in verse 39.
n.10: A region or town of Edom, known for its wise men (Job 2:11). Verses 7–22 have many lines in common with Obadiah 1–9.
n.11: Literally "go deep to dwell", that is, hide in caves. Also in verse 30. Dedan was an Arabian people southeast of Edom (25:23).
n.12: Or, as questions, as in Obadiah 5: "would they not leave gleanings? … would they not destroy only what they wanted?"
n.13: The cup of the LORD's wrath (25:15–29).
n.14: A chief city of Edom (Isaiah 34:6; Amos 1:12). Also in verse 22.
n.15: Hebrew *tiflatstekha*, a rare word, perhaps "the horror you cause".
n.16: Hebrew *sela*, "rock", perhaps also the Edomite stronghold Sela (2 Kings 14:7).
n.17: Repeated in 50:40.
n.18: Literally "the pride of the Jordan" (12:5). Verses 19–21 are repeated, of Babylon, in 50:44–46.
n.19: Hebrew *neveh etan*, "an enduring pasture".
n.20: The Hebrew of this sentence is difficult. Literally "for I will in a moment make him run from it, and who is chosen I will appoint over it".
n.21: Hebrew *yam suf*, "Sea of Reeds", here probably the Gulf of Aqaba, south of Edom.
n.24: The meaning is uncertain. Literally "How is it not abandoned". Perhaps the citizens lament that they did not leave the city in time.
n.26: The name of several kings of Damascus (1 Kings 15:18; 2 Kings 13:3). Compare Amos 1:4.
n.27: Kedar was a people of the Arabian desert (2:10). This Hazor is not the city in Galilee but probably a group of Arab settlements. Nebuchadnezzar campaigned against the Arabs in 599–598 BC.
n.28: The Hebrew text is written "against them" but read "against you".
n.30: Elam lay east of Babylonia, in what is now southwestern Iran. Zedekiah began to reign in 597 BC.
n.31: Literally "the first of their might". The Elamites were famous archers (Isaiah 22:6).
n.32: The Hebrew text is written *olam*, "forever", but read *Elam*.
n.33: Literally "in the latter end of the days".

v: The word that the LORD[^1] spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Babylonians,[^2] through Jeremiah the prophet:
הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃

Declare it among the nations and proclaim it; raise a signal flag and proclaim it; hide nothing. Say: Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered.[^3] Her images are put to shame; her idols[^4] are shattered.
הַגִּ֨ידוּ בַגּוֹיִ֤ם וְהַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ וּֽשְׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הַשְׁמִ֖יעוּ אַל־תְּכַחֵ֑דוּ אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ חַ֣ת מְרֹדָ֔ךְ הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ עֲצַבֶּ֔יהָ חַ֖תּוּ גִּלּוּלֶֽיהָ׃
For a nation from the north has come up against her; it will make her land a desolation, and no one will live in it. Both human beings and animals have fled; they are gone.
כִּ֣י עָלָה֩ עָלֶ֨יהָ גּ֜וֹי מִצָּפ֗וֹן הֽוּא־יָשִׁ֤ית אֶת־אַרְצָהּ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּ֑הּ מֵאָדָ֥ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֖ה נָ֥דוּ הָלָֽכוּ׃
In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the people of Israel will come, they and the people of Judah together. They will come weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.
בַּיָּמִ֨ים הָהֵ֜מָּה וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה יָבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הֵ֥מָּה וּבְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו הָל֤וֹךְ וּבָכוֹ֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃
They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned toward it: "Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD[^5] in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten."
צִיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֔לוּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הֵ֣נָּה פְנֵיהֶ֑ם בֹּ֚אוּ וְנִלְו֣וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃ ס
My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray, making them roam on the mountains.[^6] They have wandered from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
צֹ֤אן אֹֽבְדוֹת֙ *היה **הָי֣וּ עַמִּ֔י רֹעֵיהֶ֣ם הִתְע֔וּם הָרִ֖ים *שובבים **שֽׁוֹבְב֑וּם מֵהַ֤ר אֶל־גִּבְעָה֙ הָלָ֔כוּ שָׁכְח֖וּ רִבְצָֽם׃
All who found them have devoured them, and their foes have said, "We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, their true pasture,[^7] the LORD, the hope of their ancestors."
כָּל־מוֹצְאֵיהֶ֣ם אֲכָל֔וּם וְצָרֵיהֶ֥ם אָמְר֖וּ לֹ֣א נֶאְשָׁ֑ם תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטְא֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ נְוֵה־צֶ֔דֶק וּמִקְוֵ֥ה אֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Flee from the midst of Babylon; go out[^8] from the land of the Babylonians, and be like male goats that go before the flock.
נֻ֚דוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים *יצאו **צֵ֑אוּ וִהְי֕וּ כְּעַתּוּדִ֖ים לִפְנֵי־צֹֽאן׃

For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will draw up their lines against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like those of a skilled warrior who does not return empty-handed.
כִּ֣י הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֡י מֵעִיר֩ וּמַעֲלֶ֨ה עַל־בָּבֶ֜ל קְהַל־גּוֹיִ֤ם גְּדֹלִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְעָ֣רְכוּ לָ֔הּ מִשָּׁ֖ם תִּלָּכֵ֑ד חִצָּיו֙ כְּגִבּ֣וֹר מַשְׁכִּ֔יל לֹ֥א יָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃
Babylonia[^9] will become plunder; all who plunder her will be satisfied, declares the LORD.
וְהָיְתָ֥ה כַשְׂדִּ֖ים לְשָׁלָ֑ל כָּל־שֹׁלְלֶ֥יהָ יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Though you rejoice, though you exult, you who plunder my inheritance, though you frisk about like a heifer threshing grain[^10] and neigh like stallions,
כִּ֤י *תשמחי **תִשְׂמְחוּ֙ כִּ֣י *תעלזי **תַֽעֲלְז֔וּ שֹׁסֵ֖י נַחֲלָתִ֑י כִּ֤י *תפושי **תָפ֙וּשׁוּ֙ כְּעֶגְלָ֣ה דָשָׁ֔ה *ותצהלי **וְתִצְהֲל֖וּ כָּאֲבִּרִֽים׃
your mother will be greatly ashamed; she who bore you will be disgraced. Look, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land and a desert.
בּ֤וֹשָׁה אִמְּכֶם֙ מְאֹ֔ד חָפְרָ֖ה יֽוֹלַדְתְּכֶ֑ם הִנֵּה֙ אַחֲרִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם מִדְבָּ֖ר צִיָּ֥ה וַעֲרָבָֽה׃
Because of the wrath of the LORD she will not be inhabited, but will be completely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
מִקֶּ֤צֶף יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א תֵשֵׁ֔ב וְהָיְתָ֥ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה כֻּלָּ֑הּ כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכּוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
Draw up your lines around Babylon, all you who bend the bow! Shoot at her; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.
עִרְכ֨וּ עַל־בָּבֶ֤ל ׀ סָבִיב֙ כָּל־דֹּ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת יְד֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ אַֽל־תַּחְמְל֖וּ אֶל־חֵ֑ץ כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָֽאָה׃

Raise the battle cry against her on every side! She has surrendered;[^11] her towers[^12] have fallen; her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.
הָרִ֨יעוּ עָלֶ֤יהָ סָבִיב֙ נָתְנָ֣ה יָדָ֔הּ נָֽפְלוּ֙ *אשויתיה **אָשְׁיוֹתֶ֔יהָ נֶהֶרְס֖וּ חֽוֹמוֹתֶ֑יהָ כִּי֩ נִקְמַ֨ת יְהוָ֥ה הִיא֙ הִנָּ֣קְמוּ בָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־לָֽהּ׃

Cut off from Babylon the sower and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the oppressor,[^13] they will each turn back to their own people; they will each flee to their own land.
כִּרְת֤וּ זוֹרֵ֙עַ֙ מִבָּבֶ֔ל וְתֹפֵ֥שׂ מַגָּ֖ל בְּעֵ֣ת קָצִ֑יר מִפְּנֵי֙ חֶ֣רֶב הַיּוֹנָ֔ה אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֻֽסוּ׃ ס
Israel is a scattered sheep, chased away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at the last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has gnawed his bones.[^14]
שֶׂ֧ה פְזוּרָ֛ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲרָי֣וֹת הִדִּ֑יחוּ הָרִאשׁ֤וֹן אֲכָלוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְזֶ֤ה הָאַחֲרוֹן֙ עִצְּמ֔וֹ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃ ס
Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies,[^15] the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I punished the king of Assyria.
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֥י פֹקֵ֛ד אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקַ֖דְתִּי אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and in Bashan, and his appetite will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.
וְשֹׁבַבְתִּ֤י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־נָוֵ֔הוּ וְרָעָ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַבָּשָׁ֑ן וּבְהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֛יִם וְהַגִּלְעָ֖ד תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, search will be made for Israel's guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah's sins, but none will be found, for I will forgive those I leave as a remnant.
בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֩ וּבָעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה יְבֻקַּ֞שׁ אֶת־עֲוֺ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־חַטֹּ֥את יְהוּדָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִמָּצֶ֑אינָה כִּ֥י אֶסְלַ֖ח לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אַשְׁאִֽיר׃

Go up against the land of Merathaim, against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.[^16] Put them to the sword and devote them to destruction,[^17] declares the LORD; do all that I have commanded you.
עַל־הָאָ֤רֶץ מְרָתַ֙יִם֙ עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּק֑וֹד חֲרֹ֨ב וְהַחֲרֵ֤ם אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲשֵׂ֕ה כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִֽיךָ׃ ס
The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction!
ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְשֶׁ֖בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
אֵ֤יךְ נִגְדַּע֙ וַיִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר פַּטִּ֖ישׁ כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and seized, because you challenged the LORD.
יָקֹ֨שְׁתִּי לָ֤ךְ וְגַם־נִלְכַּדְתְּ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאַ֖תְּ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עַתְּ נִמְצֵאת֙ וְגַם־נִתְפַּ֔שְׂתְּ כִּ֥י בַֽיהוָ֖ה הִתְגָּרִֽית׃
The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Lord GOD of Armies[^18] has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.
פָּתַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־א֣וֹצָר֔וֹ וַיּוֹצֵ֖א אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י זַעְמ֑וֹ כִּי־מְלָאכָ֣ה הִ֗יא לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
Come against her from every side;[^19] open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction. Let her have no remnant left.
בֹּֽאוּ־לָ֤הּ מִקֵּץ֙ פִּתְח֣וּ מַאֲבֻסֶ֔יהָ סָלּ֥וּהָ כְמוֹ־עֲרֵמִ֖ים וְהַחֲרִימ֑וּהָ אַל־תְּהִי־לָ֖הּ שְׁאֵרִֽית׃
Put all her young bulls to the sword;[^20] let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
חִרְבוּ֙ כָּל־פָּרֶ֔יהָ יֵרְד֖וּ לַטָּ֑בַח ה֣וֹי עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־בָ֥א יוֹמָ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃ ס
Listen! Fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon are declaring in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, vengeance for his temple.
ק֥וֹל נָסִ֛ים וּפְלֵטִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ בָּבֶ֑ל לְהַגִּ֣יד בְּצִיּ֗וֹן אֶת־נִקְמַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃

Summon archers[^21] against Babylon, all who bend the bow. Camp all around her; let none of hers escape.[^22] Repay her for her deeds; do to her just as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.

הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ אֶל־בָּבֶ֣ל ׀ רַ֠בִּים כָּל־דֹּ֨רְכֵי קֶ֜שֶׁת חֲנ֧וּ עָלֶ֣יהָ סָבִ֗יב אַל־יְהִי־**לָהּ֙[t] פְּלֵטָ֔ה שַׁלְּמוּ־לָ֣הּ כְּפָעֳלָ֔הּ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־לָ֑הּ כִּ֧י אֶל־יְהוָ֛ה זָ֖דָה אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.[^23]
לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתָּ֥הּ יִדַּ֛מּוּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Look, I am against you, Arrogant One,[^24] declares the Lord GOD of Armies, for your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ זָד֔וֹן נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֛י בָּ֥א יוֹמְךָ֖ עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיךָ׃
The Arrogant One will stumble and fall, with no one to raise him up. I will set fire to his cities, and it will consume everything around him.
וְכָשַׁ֤ל זָדוֹן֙ וְנָפַ֔ל וְאֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ מֵקִ֑ים וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֖ה כָּל־סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ ס
This is what the LORD of Armies says: The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah with them. All who took them captive hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עֲשׁוּקִ֛ים בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל וּבְנֵי־יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו וְכָל־שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ בָ֔ם מֵאֲנ֖וּ שַׁלְּחָֽם׃
But their Redeemer[^25] is strong; the LORD of Armies is his name. He will surely plead their cause, so that he may give rest to the earth, but unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.[^26]
גֹּאֲלָ֣ם ׀ חָזָ֗ק יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שְׁמ֔וֹ רִ֥יב יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֑ם לְמַ֙עַן֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעַ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִרְגִּ֖יז לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃
A sword against the Babylonians, declares the LORD, and against the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!
חֶ֥רֶב עַל־כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־שָׂרֶ֖יהָ וְאֶל־חֲכָמֶֽיהָ׃
A sword against her false prophets,[^27] and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־הַבַּדִּ֖ים וְנֹאָ֑לוּ חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־גִּבּוֹרֶ֖יהָ וָחָֽתּוּ׃
A sword against his horses and his chariots, and against all the foreign troops[^28] in her midst, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
חֶ֜רֶב אֶל־סוּסָ֣יו וְאֶל־רִכְבּ֗וֹ וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעֶ֛רֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖הּ וְהָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־אוֹצְרֹתֶ֖יהָ וּבֻזָּֽזוּ׃
A drought[^29] on her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and they go mad over their terrifying images.
חֹ֥רֶב אֶל־מֵימֶ֖יהָ וְיָבֵ֑שׁוּ כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ פְּסִלִים֙ הִ֔יא וּבָאֵימִ֖ים יִתְהֹלָֽלוּ׃
Therefore desert creatures will live there with hyenas,[^30] and ostriches will live in her. She will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.
לָכֵ֗ן יֵשְׁב֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֖הּ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֥ב עוֹד֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכּ֖וֹן עַד־דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, declares the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will stay in it.[^31]
כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־סְדֹ֧ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאֶת־שְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃
Look, a people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are being stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.[^32]
הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מִצָּפ֑וֹן וְג֤וֹי גָּדוֹל֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים יֵעֹ֖רוּ מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
They grasp bow and javelin; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound is like the roaring sea; they ride on horses, drawn up like warriors for battle against you, Daughter Babylon.
קֶ֣שֶׁת וְכִידֹ֞ן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הֵ֙מָּה֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָם֙ כַּיָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְעַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת־בָּבֶֽל׃
The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor.
שָׁמַ֧ע מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־שִׁמְעָ֖ם וְרָפ֣וּ יָדָ֑יו צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

Look, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan[^33] to a pasture that is always green, I will suddenly chase them from it, and I will appoint over it whoever is chosen. For who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־אַרְגִּ֤עָה *ארוצם **אֲרִיצֵם֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֙וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יוֹעִדֶ֔נִּי וּמִֽי־זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃

Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Babylon, and the purposes he has formed against the land of the Babylonians: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely the pasture will be made desolate because of them.
לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־בָּבֶ֔ל וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים אִם־לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נָוֶֽה׃
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth quakes, and a cry is heard among the nations.
מִקּוֹל֙ נִתְפְּשָׂ֣ה בָבֶ֔ל נִרְעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וּזְעָקָ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִ֥ם נִשְׁמָֽע׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Chapters 50–51 are the last and longest of the oracles against the nations.
n.2: Hebrew *Kasdim*, traditionally "Chaldeans": the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings then ruled Babylon. Also in verses 8, 10, 25, 35 and 45.
n.3: Hebrew *Merodakh*. Marduk was the chief god of Babylon, and *Bel*, "lord", was his title.
n.4: Hebrew *gillulim*, a scornful word for idols, perhaps "dung pellets".
n.5: Literally "Come, and they will join themselves to the LORD".
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "faithless mountains" but read "they made them roam on the mountains".
n.7: Literally "the pasture of righteousness" (31:23).
n.8: The Hebrew text is written "they will go out" but read "go out".
n.9: Hebrew *Kasdim*, here meaning the land.
n.10: The same consonants can be read "like a heifer in the grass", as the Septuagint reads.
n.11: Literally "She has given her hand".
n.12: Hebrew *ashyot*, a rare word, perhaps "towers" or "foundations".
n.13: Or "the cruel sword". Hebrew *ha-yonah*, perhaps "the oppressor" (46:16).
n.14: Literally "has broken his bones". Assyria destroyed the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6), and Babylon took Judah into exile.
n.15: *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verses 25, 31, 33 and 34.
n.16: Two wordplays. *Merathaim*, "double rebellion", sounds like *mat marrati*, a Babylonian name for the region at the head of the Persian Gulf. *Pekod*, "punishment", was an Aramean people in eastern Babylonia (Ezekiel 23:23).
n.17: Literally "Put to the sword and devote to destruction after them". Hebrew *charam*: see 25:9. Also in verse 26.
n.18: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH tseva'ot*, "my Lord YHWH of Armies". Also in verse 31.
n.19: Literally "from the end".
n.20: Her *young bulls* are her warriors (compare 46:21).
n.22: The words "of hers" are read but not written in the Hebrew text.
n.23: Verse 30 repeats 49:26, there said of Damascus.
n.24: Hebrew *zadon*, "arrogance", used as a name for Babylon. Also in verse 32.
n.25: Hebrew *go'el*, a kinsman who buys back a relative or his property (31:11).
n.27: Hebrew *baddim*, "empty talkers", probably her diviners (compare Isaiah 44:25).
n.28: Hebrew *ha-erev*, "the mixture" (25:20), here probably foreign soldiers.
n.29: Hebrew *chorev*, "drought", a play on *cherev*, "sword", in verses 35–37.
n.30: The meaning of the Hebrew words *tsiyyim* and *iyyim* is uncertain. Compare Isaiah 13:21–22; 34:14.
n.31: Verse 40 repeats 49:18, there said of Edom.
n.32: Verses 41–43 repeat 6:22–24, there said of Jerusalem.
n.33: Literally "the pride of the Jordan". Verses 44–46 repeat 49:19–21, there said of Edom.

v: This is what the LORD[^1] says: I am going to stir up a destroying wind[^2] against Babylon and against the people who live in Leb-kamai.[^3]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי֙ מֵעִ֣יר עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י לֵ֣ב קָמָ֑י ר֖וּחַ מַשְׁחִֽית׃
I will send foreigners to Babylon, and they will winnow her[^4] and empty her land, for they will come against her from every side on the day of disaster.
וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֤ל ׀ זָרִים֙ וְזֵר֔וּהָ וִיבֹקְק֖וּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֑הּ כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מִסָּבִ֖יב בְּי֥וֹם רָעָֽה׃
Against the archer let the archer bend his bow, and against the one who stands up in his armor.[^5] Do not spare her young men; devote her whole army to destruction.[^6]
אֶֽל־יִדְרֹ֤ךְ *ידרך הַדֹּרֵךְ֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־יִתְעַ֖ל בְּסִרְיֹנּ֑וֹ וְאַֽל־תַּחְמְלוּ֙ אֶל־בַּ֣חֻרֶ֔יהָ הַחֲרִ֖ימוּ כָּל־צְבָאָֽהּ׃
They will fall slain in the land of the Babylonians,[^7] pierced through in her streets.
וְנָפְל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וּמְדֻקָּרִ֖ים בְּחוּצוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed by their God, by the LORD of Armies,[^8] though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.[^9]
כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אַלְמָ֨ן יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וִֽיהוּדָה֙ מֵֽאֱלֹהָ֔יו מֵֽיְהוָ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֤י אַרְצָם֙ מָלְאָ֣ה אָשָׁ֔ם מִקְּד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Flee from the midst of Babylon! Save your lives, each of you! Do not be destroyed[^10] because of her guilt. For this is the time of the LORD's vengeance; he is repaying her what she deserves.
נֻ֣סוּ ׀ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֗ל וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ אַל־תִּדַּ֖מּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּי֩ עֵ֨ת נְקָמָ֥ה הִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה גְּמ֕וּל ה֥וּא מְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לָֽהּ׃
Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad.[^11]
כּוֹס־זָהָ֤ב בָּבֶל֙ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁכֶּ֖רֶת כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ מִיֵּינָהּ֙ שָׁת֣וּ גוֹיִ֔ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִתְהֹלְל֥וּ גוֹיִֽם׃
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered.[^12] Wail for her! Get balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
פִּתְאֹ֛ם נָפְלָ֥ה בָבֶ֖ל וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ עָלֶ֗יהָ קְח֤וּ צֳרִי֙ לְמַכְאוֹבָ֔הּ אוּלַ֖י תֵּרָפֵֽא׃
"We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Leave her, and let us each go to our own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and rises as high as the clouds.[^13]
*רפאנו **רִפִּ֤ינוּ אֶת־בָּבֶל֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְפָּ֔תָה עִזְב֕וּהָ וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ כִּֽי־נָגַ֤ע אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מִשְׁפָּטָ֔הּ וְנִשָּׂ֖א עַד־שְׁחָקִֽים׃
The LORD has brought our vindication to light.[^14] Come, let us tell in Zion the work of the LORD our God."
הוֹצִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ בֹּ֚אוּ וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה בְצִיּ֔וֹן אֶֽת־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers![^15] The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes,[^16] because his purpose is to destroy Babylon. For this is the vengeance of the LORD, vengeance for his temple.
הָבֵ֣רוּ הַחִצִּים֮ מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒ הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ר֙וּחַ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י כִּֽי־עַל־בָּבֶ֥ל מְזִמָּת֖וֹ לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֑הּ כִּֽי־נִקְמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃

Raise a signal flag against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the watch; post the watchmen; prepare the ambushes! For the LORD has both planned and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
אֶל־חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ־נֵ֗ס הַחֲזִ֙יקוּ֙ הַמִּשְׁמָ֔ר הָקִ֙ימוּ֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים הָכִ֖ינוּ הָאֹֽרְבִ֑ים כִּ֚י גַּם־זָמַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה גַּם־עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃
You who live by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your life is cut off.[^17]
*שכנתי **שֹׁכַנְתְּ֙ עַל־מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים רַבַּ֖ת אֽוֹצָרֹ֑ת בָּ֥א קִצֵּ֖ךְ אַמַּ֥ת בִּצְעֵֽךְ׃
The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with people like a swarm of locusts, and they will raise the shout of victory[^18] over you.
נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־מִלֵּאתִ֤יךְ אָדָם֙ כַּיֶּ֔לֶק וְעָנ֥וּ עָלַ֖יִךְ הֵידָֽד׃ ס
He made the earth by his power; he established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.[^19]
עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנָת֖וֹ נָטָ֥ה שָׁמָֽיִם׃
When he thunders,[^20] there is a roar of waters in the heavens; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֙יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּ֥עַל נְשִׂאִ֖ים מִקְצֵה־אָ֑רֶץ בְּרָקִ֤ים לַמָּטָר֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיֹּ֥צֵא ר֖וּחַ מֵאֹצְרֹתָֽיו׃
Every human being is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol. For his cast images are a lie; there is no breath in them.
נִבְעַ֤ר כָּל־אָדָם֙ מִדַּ֔עַת הֹבִ֥ישׁ כָּל־צֹרֵ֖ף מִפָּ֑סֶל כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר נִסְכּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ר֥וּחַ בָּֽם׃
They are worthless, a work of mockery. At the time of their punishment they will perish.
הֶ֣בֶל הֵ֔מָּה מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה תַּעְתֻּעִ֑ים בְּעֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the maker of all things, and of the tribe that is his inheritance.[^21] The LORD of Armies is his name.
לֹֽא־כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲק֗וֹב כִּֽי־יוֹצֵ֤ר הַכֹּל֙ ה֔וּא וְשֵׁ֖בֶט נַחֲלָת֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ ס
You are my war club, my weapon for battle:[^22] with you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms;
מַפֵּץ־אַתָּ֣ה לִ֔י כְּלֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִשְׁחַתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃
with you I shatter the horse and its rider; with you I shatter the chariot and its driver;
וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ ס֖וּס וְרֹֽכְב֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ רֶ֖כֶב וְרֹכְבֽוֹ׃
with you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter the old and the young; with you I shatter the young man and the young woman;
וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ זָקֵ֣ן וָנָ֑עַר וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ בָּח֖וּר וּבְתוּלָֽה׃
with you I shatter the shepherd and his flock; with you I shatter the farmer and his team; with you I shatter governors and deputies.[^23]
וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ רֹעֶ֣ה וְעֶדְר֔וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ אִכָּ֣ר וְצִמְדּ֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ פַּח֖וֹת וּסְגָנִֽים׃
I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Babylonia[^24] for all the evil they have done in Zion before your eyes, declares the LORD.
וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל וּלְכֹ֣ל ׀ יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֗ים אֵ֧ת כָּל־רָעָתָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֥וּ בְצִיּ֖וֹן לְעֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ ס

Look, I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD, you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the cliffs and make you a burned-out mountain.
הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה הַמַּשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנָטִ֨יתִי אֶת־יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וְגִלְגַּלְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִן־הַסְּלָעִ֔ים וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְהַ֥ר שְׂרֵפָֽה׃
No stone will be taken from you for a cornerstone, nor any stone for a foundation, for you will be desolate forever, declares the LORD.
וְלֹֽא־יִקְח֤וּ מִמְּךָ֙ אֶ֣בֶן לְפִנָּ֔ה וְאֶ֖בֶן לְמֽוֹסָד֑וֹת כִּֽי־שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֛ם תִּֽהְיֶ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

Raise a signal flag in the land! Blow the ram's horn among the nations! Prepare the nations for war against her;[^25] summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz.[^26] Appoint a commander[^27] against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.[^28]

שְׂאוּ־נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֤ר בַּגּוֹיִם֙ קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם הַשְׁמִ֧יעוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מַמְלְכ֥וֹת אֲרָרַ֖ט מִנִּ֣י וְאַשְׁכְּנָ֑ז פִּקְד֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ טִפְסָ֔ר הַֽעֲלוּ־ס֖וּס כְּיֶ֥לֶק סָמָֽר׃
Prepare the nations for war against her, the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their deputies, and every land under their rule.
קַדְּשׁ֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ גוֹיִם֙ אֶת־מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י אֶת־פַּחוֹתֶ֖יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־סְגָנֶ֑יהָ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃
The earth quakes and writhes, for the LORD's purposes against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a desolation, with no one living in it.
וַתִּרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ וַתָּחֹ֑ל כִּ֣י קָ֤מָה עַל־בָּבֶל֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה לָשׂ֞וּם אֶת־אֶ֧רֶץ בָּבֶ֛ל לְשַׁמָּ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they stay in their strongholds. Their strength has failed; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.
חָדְלוּ֩ גִבּוֹרֵ֨י בָבֶ֜ל לְהִלָּחֵ֗ם יָֽשְׁבוּ֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת נָשְׁתָ֥ה גְבוּרָתָ֖ם הָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים הִצִּ֥יתוּ מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶ֖יהָ נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ בְרִיחֶֽיהָ׃
Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end,
רָ֤ץ לִקְרַאת־רָץ֙ יָר֔וּץ וּמַגִּ֖יד לִקְרַ֣את מַגִּ֑יד לְהַגִּיד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל כִּֽי־נִלְכְּדָ֥ה עִיר֖וֹ מִקָּצֶֽה׃
the fords have been seized, the marshes[^29] set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified.
וְהַמַּעְבָּר֣וֹת נִתְפָּ֔שׂוּ וְאֶת־הָאֲגַמִּ֖ים שָׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֑שׁ וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה נִבְהָֽלוּ׃ ס
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; in a little while the time of her harvest will come.
כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּת־בָּבֶ֕ל כְּגֹ֖רֶן עֵ֣ת הִדְרִיכָ֑הּ ע֣וֹד מְעַ֔ט וּבָ֥אָה עֵֽת־הַקָּצִ֖יר לָֽהּ׃

"Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me;[^30] he has crushed me; he has set me down like an empty jar. He has swallowed me like a sea monster;[^31] he has filled his belly with my delicacies and rinsed me out."[^32]
*אכלנו **אֲכָלַ֣נִי *הממנו **הֲמָמַ֗נִי נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶל֒ *הציגנו **הִצִּיגַ֙נִי֙ כְּלִ֣י רִ֔יק *בלענו **בְּלָעַ֙נִי֙ כַּתַּנִּ֔ין מִלָּ֥א כְרֵשׂ֖וֹ מֵֽעֲדָנָ֑י *הדיחנו **הֱדִיחָֽנִי׃
"May the violence done to me and to my flesh[^33] be on Babylon," the people of Zion will say. "May my blood be on the inhabitants of Babylonia," Jerusalem will say.
חֲמָסִ֤י וּשְׁאֵרִי֙ עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל תֹּאמַ֖ר יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן וְדָמִי֙ אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֔ים תֹּאמַ֖ר יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to plead your cause and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea[^34] and make her spring run dry.
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי־רָב֙ אֶת־רִיבֵ֔ךְ וְנִקַּמְתִּ֖י אֶת־נִקְמָתֵ֑ךְ וְהַחֲרַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־יַמָּ֔הּ וְהֹבַשְׁתִּ֖י אֶת־מְקוֹרָֽהּ׃
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a thing to hiss at, with no one living there.
וְהָיְתָה֩ בָבֶ֨ל ׀ לְגַלִּ֧ים ׀ מְעוֹן־תַּנִּ֛ים שַׁמָּ֥ה וּשְׁרֵקָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
They roar together like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.
יַחְדָּ֖ו כַּכְּפִרִ֣ים יִשְׁאָ֑גוּ נָעֲר֖וּ כְּגוֹרֵ֥י אֲרָיֽוֹת׃
While they are heated, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they celebrate, then sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake, declares the LORD.
בְּחֻמָּ֞ם אָשִׁ֣ית אֶת־מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֗ם וְהִשְׁכַּרְתִּים֙ לְמַ֣עַן יַעֲלֹ֔זוּ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
אֽוֹרִידֵ֖ם כְּכָרִ֣ים לִטְב֑וֹחַ כְּאֵילִ֖ים עִם־עַתּוּדִֽים׃
How Sheshach[^35] is captured, the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
אֵ֚יךְ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה שֵׁשַׁ֔ךְ וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
The sea has risen over Babylon; she is covered with its roaring waves.
עָלָ֥ה עַל־בָּבֶ֖ל הַיָּ֑ם בַּהֲמ֥וֹן גַּלָּ֖יו נִכְסָֽתָה׃
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one lives, through which no human being passes.
הָי֤וּ עָרֶ֙יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ צִיָּ֣ה וַעֲרָבָ֑ה אֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּהֵן֙ כָּל־אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֥ר בָּהֵ֖ן בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃
I will punish Bel[^36] in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed.[^37] The nations will no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Babylon has fallen.
וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עַל־בֵּ֜ל בְּבָבֶ֗ל וְהֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶת־בִּלְעוֹ֙ מִפִּ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יִנְהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו ע֖וֹד גּוֹיִ֑ם גַּם־חוֹמַ֥ת בָּבֶ֖ל נָפָֽלָה׃
Go out from her midst, my people! Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD![^38]
צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י וּמַלְּט֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־יְהוָֽה׃
Do not lose heart or be afraid at the rumors heard in the land, when one rumor comes this year and another the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler.
וּפֶן־יֵרַ֤ךְ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְתִֽירְא֔וּ בַּשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה הַנִּשְׁמַ֣עַת בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּבָ֧א בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמוּעָ֗ה וְאַחֲרָ֤יו בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֔ה וְחָמָ֣ס בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל עַל־מֹשֵֽׁל׃
Therefore, look, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וּפָקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־פְּסִילֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ תֵּב֑וֹשׁ וְכָל־חֲלָלֶ֖יהָ יִפְּל֥וּ בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃
Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for the destroyers will come against her from the north, declares the LORD.
וְרִנְּנ֤וּ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֔רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֧י מִצָּפ֛וֹן יָבוֹא־לָ֥הּ הַשּׁוֹדְדִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Babylon must fall because of the slain of Israel, as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
גַּם־בָּבֶ֕ל לִנְפֹּ֖ל חַֽלְלֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־לְבָבֶ֥ל נָפְל֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to your mind.
פְּלֵטִ֣ים מֵחֶ֔רֶב הִלְכ֖וּ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ זִכְר֤וּ מֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וִירֽוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם תַּעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־לְבַבְכֶֽם׃
"We are ashamed, for we have heard insults; disgrace has covered our faces, for foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's house."[^39]
בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ חֶרְפָּ֔ה כִּסְּתָ֥ה כְלִמָּ֖ה פָּנֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֚י בָּ֣אוּ זָרִ֔ים עַֽל־מִקְדְּשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֖י עַל־פְּסִילֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ יֶאֱנֹ֥ק חָלָֽל׃
Though Babylon should climb to the heavens, and though she should fortify her lofty stronghold, destroyers will come against her from me, declares the LORD.
כִּֽי־תַעֲלֶ֤ה בָבֶל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכִ֥י תְבַצֵּ֖ר מְר֣וֹם עֻזָּ֑הּ מֵאִתִּ֗י יָבֹ֧אוּ שֹׁדְדִ֛ים לָ֖הּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Listen! A cry from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylonians!
ק֥וֹל זְעָקָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and silencing her great noise. Their waves roar like many waters; the sound of their voice resounds.
כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאִבַּ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וְהָמ֤וּ גַלֵּיהֶם֙ כְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים נִתַּ֥ן שְׁא֖וֹן קוֹלָֽם׃
For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her warriors are captured; their bows are shattered. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will surely repay.
כִּי֩ בָ֨א עָלֶ֤יהָ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד וְנִלְכְּדוּ֙ גִּבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ חִתְּתָ֖ה קַשְּׁתוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֧ל גְּמֻל֛וֹת יְהוָ֖ה שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃
I will make her officials and her wise men drunk, her governors, her deputies and her warriors; they will sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
וְ֠הִשְׁכַּרְתִּי שָׂרֶ֨יהָ וַחֲכָמֶ֜יהָ פַּחוֹתֶ֤יהָ וּסְגָנֶ֙יהָ֙ וְגִבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֨ם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ ס

This is what the LORD of Armies says: The thick wall of Babylon[^40] will be leveled to the ground, and her high gates set on fire. The peoples exhaust themselves for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the fire.[^41]

כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת חֹ֠מוֹת בָּבֶ֤ל הָֽרְחָבָה֙ עַרְעֵ֣ר תִּתְעַרְעָ֔ר וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ הַגְּבֹהִ֖ים בָּאֵ֣שׁ יִצַּ֑תּוּ וְיִֽגְע֨וּ עַמִּ֧ים בְּדֵי־רִ֛יק וּלְאֻמִּ֥ים בְּדֵי־אֵ֖שׁ וְיָעֵֽפוּ׃ ס

This is the command that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign.[^42] Seraiah was the quartermaster.[^43]

הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה ׀ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶת־שְׂרָיָ֣ה בֶן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ בְּלֶכְתּ֞וֹ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה שַׂ֥ר מְנוּחָֽה׃
Jeremiah had written on one scroll all the disaster that would come on Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אֵ֧ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־סֵ֣פֶר אֶחָ֑ד אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים אֶל־בָּבֶֽל׃
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud.
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־שְׂרָיָ֑ה כְּבֹאֲךָ֣ בָבֶ֔ל וְֽרָאִ֔יתָ וְֽקָרָ֔אתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
Then say, 'LORD, you have said concerning this place that you will cut it off, so that no one will live in it, neither human beings nor animals, for it will be desolate forever.'
וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ יְהוָה֙ אַתָּ֨ה דִבַּ֜רְתָּ אֶל־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לְהַכְרִית֔וֹ לְבִלְתִּ֤י הֱיֽוֹת־בּוֹ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב לְמֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה כִּֽי־שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃
When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates.
וְהָיָה֙ כְּכַלֹּ֣תְךָ֔ לִקְרֹ֖א אֶת־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה תִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ אֶ֔בֶן וְהִשְׁלַכְתּ֖וֹ אֶל־תּ֥וֹךְ פְּרָֽת׃
Then say, 'So will Babylon sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I am going to bring on her. And they will grow weary.'"[^44] Thus far the words of Jeremiah.
וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כָּ֠כָה תִּשְׁקַ֨ע בָּבֶ֤ל וְלֹֽא־תָקוּם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ וְיָעֵ֑פוּ עַד־הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Or "the spirit of a destroyer". Hebrew *ruach*, "wind, spirit".
n.3: *Leb-kamai*, "the heart of those who rise against me", is a code name for *Kasdim*, Chaldea, made by the cipher *atbash* (see 25:26), in which each letter is replaced by the letter in the same place counting from the end of the alphabet. So *k-s-d-y* becomes *l-b-q-m-y*. The Septuagint reads "the Chaldeans".
n.4: A wordplay: *zarim*, "foreigners", and *zeruha*, "they will winnow her". The same consonants can be read *zorim*, "winnowers".
n.5: The Hebrew of these lines is difficult. Some scholars read *al*, "Let not the archer bend his bow, and let him not stand up in his armor", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.6: Hebrew *charam*: see 25:9.
n.7: Hebrew *Kasdim*, traditionally "Chaldeans": the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings then ruled Babylon. Also in verses 24, 35 and 54.
n.8: *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verses 14, 19, 33, 57 and 58.
n.9: *Their land* may be the land of Israel and Judah, or the land of the Babylonians.
n.10: Or "Do not be silenced".
n.11: Compare 25:15–29. Revelation 17:2–4 and 18:3 take up this picture.
n.12: Compare Isaiah 21:9 and Revelation 14:8; 18:2.
n.13: The speakers in verses 9–10 are probably the foreigners living in Babylon, and then the exiles of Judah.
n.14: Literally "has brought out our righteousnesses".
n.15: Hebrew *shelatim*, perhaps "quivers" or "shields".
n.16: The Medes, from what is now northwestern Iran, joined the Persians under Cyrus, who took Babylon in 539 BC. Also in verse 28.
n.17: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "the cubit of your cutting off", perhaps the length of your life, like cloth cut from the loom (Isaiah 38:12).
n.18: Hebrew *hedad*, the shout of grape treaders (25:30; 48:33).
n.19: Verses 15–19 repeat 10:12–16.
n.20: Literally "At the sound of his giving".
n.21: Literally "and the tribe of his inheritance". 10:16 reads "and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance".
n.22: *You* may be Babylon, the LORD's instrument until now, or the conqueror who is coming against her. The verb *naphats*, "shatter", is repeated nine times in verses 20–23.
