n.23: Hebrew *pachot* and *seganim*, titles of officials in the Babylonian and Persian empires. Also in verses 28 and 57.
n.24: Hebrew *Kasdim*, here meaning the land. Also in verse 35.
n.25: Literally "Consecrate nations against her", from the religious rites that opened a campaign (6:4). Also in verse 28.
n.26: Ararat (Urartu), Minni (the Mannaeans) and Ashkenaz (probably the Scythians) were peoples of the mountains north of Mesopotamia.
n.27: Hebrew *tifsar*, a word borrowed from the Babylonian language, "official".
n.28: Hebrew *yeleq samar*, perhaps locusts at a stage when their wings are still sheathed.
n.29: Hebrew *agammim*, "reed marshes", perhaps the reed thickets or defenses along the river.
n.30: The Hebrew text is written "us" throughout this verse but read "me". Jerusalem speaks in verses 34–35.
n.31: Hebrew *tannin*, a sea monster or dragon.
n.34: Her *sea* may be the Euphrates with its canals.
n.35: *Sheshach* is a code name for Babylon made by the cipher *atbash*: see 25:26 and verse 1.
n.36: A title of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon (50:2).
n.37: The Septuagint does not have the rest of verse 44, or verses 45–48 and the first half of verse 49.
n.39: The exiles answer in this verse.
n.40: Literally "the walls of Babylon, the broad".
n.41: Habakkuk 2:13 has nearly the same words.
n.42: In 594–593 BC. Seraiah was the brother of Baruch son of Neriah (32:12).
n.43: Hebrew *sar menuchah*, "officer of the resting place", perhaps the officer in charge of the stopping places on the journey.
n.44: These words repeat the end of verse 58. They seem to have been copied here to mark where the words of Jeremiah end.

v: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king,[^1] and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal[^2] daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ *חמיטל **חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה׃
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD,[^3] just as Jehoiakim had done.[^4]
וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים׃
For it was because of the LORD's anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
כִּ֣י ׀ עַל־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּירוּשָׁלַ֣͏ִם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַד־הִשְׁלִיכ֥וֹ אוֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

So in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month,[^5] Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped against it, and they built siege works all around it.

וַיְהִי֩ בַשָּׁנָ֨ה הַתְּשִׁעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ בָּ֠א נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל ה֤וּא וְכָל־חֵילוֹ֙ עַל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּבְנ֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ דָּיֵ֖ק סָבִֽיב׃
The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצ֑וֹר עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃
In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month,[^6] the famine in the city was so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.
בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בָּעִ֑יר וְלֹא־הָיָ֥ה לֶ֖חֶם לְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the soldiers fled and went out of the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, though the Babylonians[^7] were all around the city. They went off in the direction of the Arabah.[^8]

וַתִּבָּקַ֣ע הָעִ֗יר וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֡ה יִבְרְחוּ֩ וַיֵּצְא֨וּ מֵהָעִ֜יר לַ֗יְלָה דֶּ֜רֶךְ שַׁ֤עַר בֵּין־הַחֹמֹתַ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־גַּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכַשְׂדִּ֥ים עַל־הָעִ֖יר סָבִ֑יב וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָֽה׃
But the Babylonian army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ חֵיל־כַּשְׂדִּים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּשִּׂ֥יגוּ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת יְרֵח֑וֹ וְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ נָפֹ֖צוּ מֵעָלָֽיו׃
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath,[^9] and he passed sentence on him.
וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל־מֶ֧לֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל רִבְלָ֖תָה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּטִֽים׃
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.[^10]
וַיִּשְׁחַ֧ט מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ לְעֵינָ֑יו וְגַ֛ם אֶת־כָּל־שָׂרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה שָׁחַ֥ט בְּרִבְלָֽתָה׃
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze shackles, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in prison[^11] until the day of his death.
וְאֶת־עֵינֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִוֵּ֑ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בַֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֗יִם וַיְבִאֵ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ בָּבֶ֔לָה וַיִּתְּנֵ֥הוּ *בבית־**בֵֽית־הַפְּקֻדֹּ֖ת עַד־י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ׃

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month,[^12] which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard,[^13] who served the king of Babylon,[^14] came to Jerusalem.

וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הֽ͏ַחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ הִ֗יא שְׁנַת֙ תְּשַֽׁע־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֑ל בָּ֗א נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב־טַבָּחִ֔ים עָמַ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
He burned the house of the LORD,[^15] the king's palace and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.
וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־בָּתֵּ֧י יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם וְאֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֥ית הַגָּד֖וֹל שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
The whole Babylonian army that was with the commander of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.
וְאֶת־כָּל־חֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל־חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶת־רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃

Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard deported some of the poorest of the people,[^16] the rest of the people who were left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.[^17]
וּמִדַּלּ֨וֹת הָעָ֜ם וְֽאֶת־יֶ֥תֶר הָעָ֣ם ׀ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר וְאֶת־הַנֹּֽפְלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽפְלוּ֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת יֶ֣תֶר הָֽאָמ֑וֹן הֶגְלָ֕ה נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃
But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left some of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and the fields.
וּמִדַּלּ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֕יר נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֑ים לְכֹרְמִ֖ים וּלְיֹגְבִֽים׃
The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars that belonged to the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
וְאֶת־עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְבֵית־יְהוָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־הַמְּכֹנ֞וֹת וְאֶת־יָ֧ם הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֖ה שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־כָּל־נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃
They also took away the pots, the shovels, the wick trimmers, the sprinkling bowls, the dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.
וְאֶת־הַ֠סִּרוֹת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֨ים וְאֶת־הַֽמְזַמְּר֜וֹת וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָקֹ֣ת וְאֶת־הַכַּפּ֔וֹת וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־כְּלֵ֧י הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר־יְשָׁרְת֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם לָקָֽחוּ׃

The commander of the guard took away the basins, the firepans, the sprinkling bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the dishes and the bowls for drink offerings,[^18] whatever was made of gold and whatever was made of silver.

וְאֶת־הַ֠סִּפִּים וְאֶת־הַמַּחְתּ֨וֹת וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָק֜וֹת וְאֶת־הַסִּיר֣וֹת וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹר֗וֹת וְאֶת־הַכַּפּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־הַמְּנַקִי֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר זָהָב֙ זָהָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֖סֶף כָּ֑סֶף לָקַ֖ח רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃

As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands,[^19] which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these articles was beyond weighing.

הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים ׀ שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם אֶחָד֙ וְהַבָּקָ֞ר שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֣חַת הַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
As for the pillars, each pillar was eighteen cubits[^20] high, and a cord of twelve cubits went around it. It was four fingers thick,[^21] and hollow.
וְהָעַמּוּדִ֗ים שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ *קומה **קוֹמַת֙ הָעַמֻּ֣ד הָאֶחָ֔ד וְח֛וּט שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה יְסֻבֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָבְי֛וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע אַצְבָּע֖וֹת נָבֽוּב׃
The bronze capital on top of it was five cubits high,[^22] with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was the same.
וְכֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֜יו נְחֹ֗שֶׁת וְקוֹמַ֨ת הַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הָאַחַת֮ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּוֹת֒ וּשְׂבָכָ֨ה וְרִמּוֹנִ֧ים עַֽל־הַכּוֹתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַכֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְכָאֵ֛לֶּה לַֽעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִ֖י וְרִמּוֹנִֽים׃
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides;[^23] all the pomegranates around the network numbered a hundred.
וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ הָֽרִמֹּנִ֔ים תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֖ה ר֑וּחָה כָּל־הָרִמּוֹנִ֥ים מֵאָ֛ה עַל־הַשְּׂבָכָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃
The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest and the three doorkeepers.[^24]
וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב־טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת־שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת־צְפַנְיָ֖ה כֹּהֵ֣ן הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת־שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף׃

From the city he took an official who was in charge of the soldiers, and seven of the king's advisers[^25] who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army,[^26] who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.

וּמִן־הָעִ֡יר לָקַח֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה פָקִ֣יד ׀ עַל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרֹאֵ֤י פְנֵי־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְא֣וּ בָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֗ת סֹפֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א הַמַּצְבִּ֖א אֶת־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעִֽיר׃
Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
וַיִּקַּ֣ח אוֹתָ֔ם נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֑ים וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אוֹתָ֛ם אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה׃
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אוֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar deported:[^27] in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans;[^28]
זֶ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶגְלָ֖ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֕בַע יְהוּדִ֕ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, 832 people from Jerusalem;[^29]
בִּשְׁנַ֛ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נֶ֕פֶשׁ שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם׃
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard deported 745 Judeans.[^30] In all there were 4,600 people.

בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שָׁלֹ֣שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים֮ לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֒ הֶגְלָ֗ה נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב־טַבָּחִ֔ים יְהוּדִ֕ים נֶ֕פֶשׁ שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑ה כָּל־נֶ֕פֶשׁ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃ פ

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month,[^31] Evil-merodach[^32] king of Babylon, in the year he became king, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.[^33]

וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּצֵ֥א אוֹת֖וֹ מִבֵּ֥ית *הכליא **הַכְּלֽוּא׃
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־כִּסְא֔וֹ מִמַּ֗עַל לְכִסֵּ֧א *מלכים **הַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃
So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he regularly ate at the king's table.
וְשִׁנָּ֕ה אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם לְפָנָ֛יו תָּמִ֖יד כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃
As for his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day, until the day of his death, for as long as he lived.[^34]
וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַת֩ תָּמִ֨יד נִתְּנָה־לּ֜וֹ מֵאֵ֧ת מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמ֖וֹ עַד־י֣וֹם מוֹת֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃

n.1: This chapter is also found, with small differences, in 2 Kings 24:18–25:30, except for verses 28–30, which only Jeremiah has. Verses 4–16 are also told, more briefly, in 39:1–10. The differences that change the sense are given in the notes.
n.2: Her father is not Jeremiah the prophet.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: The Septuagint does not have verses 2–3.
n.5: In January 588 BC.
n.6: In July 587 or 586 BC. 2 Kings 25:3 does not have "In the fourth month".
n.7: Hebrew *Kasdim*, traditionally "Chaldeans": the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings then ruled Babylon. Also in verses 8, 14 and 17.
n.8: The Jordan Valley. 2 Kings 25:4 has no verb for the soldiers, and reads "he went off", meaning the king.
n.9: Riblah was on the Orontes River in Syria, where Nebuchadnezzar had his headquarters. 2 Kings 25:6 does not have "in the land of Hamath", and reads "they passed sentence on him".
n.10: 2 Kings 25:7 does not mention the killing of the officials.
n.11: Literally "the house of the punishments". 2 Kings 25:7 does not mention his imprisonment or his death.
n.12: In the summer of 587 or 586 BC. 2 Kings 25:8 reads "on the seventh day of the month".
n.13: Hebrew *rav-tabbachim*, literally "chief of the butchers" or "chief of the cooks", a title of the commander of the royal bodyguard. Also in verses 14–16, 19, 24, 26 and 30.
n.14: Literally "who stood before the king of Babylon". 2 Kings 25:8 reads "an officer of the king of Babylon".
n.15: "The house of the LORD" is the temple.
n.16: These words are not in 2 Kings 25:11, and they seem to conflict with verse 16. The Septuagint does not have verse 15.
n.17: Hebrew *ha-amon*, perhaps "the craftsmen". 2 Kings 25:11 reads *he-hamon*, "the population".
n.18: 2 Kings 25:15 names only the firepans and the sprinkling bowls.
n.19: 2 Kings 25:16 does not mention the bulls. According to 1 Kings 7:25 the twelve bulls stood under the Sea, not under the stands, and King Ahaz had already taken the Sea down from them (2 Kings 16:17).
n.20: A cubit was about 18 inches (45 cm). Eighteen cubits was about 27 feet (8.1 meters), and twelve cubits about 18 feet (5.4 meters). Verses 21–23 are not in 2 Kings 25, which gives only the height of the pillars and their capitals. Compare 1 Kings 7:15–22.
n.22: About 7½ feet (2.3 meters), as in 1 Kings 7:16. 2 Kings 25:17 reads "three cubits".
n.23: Hebrew *ruchah*, "toward the wind", perhaps "on the outside" or "exposed to view". The meaning is uncertain.
n.25: Literally "of those who saw the king's face". 2 Kings 25:19 reads "five".
n.26: Or "the secretary, the commander of the army".
n.27: Verses 28–30 are found only here, and the Septuagint does not have them.
n.28: In 597 BC. 2 Kings 24:12 dates this deportation to Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year, and 2 Kings 24:14–16 gives larger numbers. Hebrew *yehudim*, the people of Judah. Also in verse 30.
n.29: In 587 or 586 BC, when Jerusalem fell. Verse 12 calls that year Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth.
n.30: In 582 or 581 BC. This deportation is not mentioned anywhere else.
n.31: In 561 BC. 2 Kings 25:27 reads "on the twenty-seventh day of the month".
n.32: Amel-Marduk, son of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon from 562 to 560 BC.
n.33: Literally "lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him out of the prison house" (compare Genesis 40:13, 20). 2 Kings 25:27 does not have "and brought him out".
n.34: Literally "all the days of his life". 2 Kings 25:30 reads "by the king", and does not have "until the day of his death".
